correctness.rationale: Rodrigues and Stieltjes integration identify the BV coefficient functional norm as max_t φ(t)|He_{n−1}(t)|/sqrt(n!), attained by a half-line unit jump. The Hermite ODE for y=φ He_{n−1} has Sonin energy E=y²+(y′)²/n with E′=−(2x/n)(y′)², proving maxima at zero for odd n and the first ± positive zeros of He_n for even n. The odd central-binomial formula and even exact root formula follow; rescale central even solution z(s), z″+(s/n)z′+z=0, with sin perturbation to calculate t_n=π/(2sqrt n)−π/(8n^(3/2))+O(n^(−5/2)) and parity-dependent O(1/n) corrections to K n^(−3/4). Independently evaluated Hermite zeros/norms for even n up to 400 and confirmed convergence of normalized two-term approximations. Finite checks do not prove the ODE perturbation for all n. The original exact one-coefficient norm and maximizing jump claims are mathematically correct.
